newsitem.title: SPAIN: Madrid stocks resume climb, volumes low.
newsitem.headline: Madrid stocks resume climb, volumes low.

text.p: Madrid shares regained momentum late in the afternoon on Thursday, but traders said the rise seemed exaggerated given that little fresh had happened to push the bourse higher.
"To me it seems that the move is a bit exaggerated, but it seems that people are again committing to a higher market. Fund money continues to enter and outlook is positive," a futures dealer said.
The Madrid general index closed up 8.77 points, or 1.57 percent, to 566.24. The Ibex-35 rose 103.00 points, or 1.61 percent, to 6,514,40 points.

Despite the rise, volumes were low as traders awaited fresh news on progress toward Europe's single currency as Germany tried to plug its budget deficit and the profile of France's new government became more clear.
Telefonica de Espana, Spain's most capitalised share, benefitted as usual from the trend higher, as investors turned to the safe bet. It ended 100 points, or 2.37 percent higher, at 4,315.
Repsol benefitted from news net cash flow rose 20 percent in the first four months of the year. Shares rose 90 pesetas, or 1.45 percent, to 6,290 pesetas.
Constructors OCP and Gines Navarro were the market's star performers ending up nearly 15 percent on merger specifics.
